The decentralized liquidity yield project Penpie was attacked, resulting in nearly $30 million in losses. According to the analysis by the SlowMist security team, the core issue of this incident lies in Penpie’s erroneous assumption that all markets created by Pendle Finance are legitimate when registering new Pendle markets. However, Pendle Finance’s market creation process is open, allowing anyone to create a market with customizable key parameters such as the SY contract address. Penpie lost approximately $27M on September 3, 2024, after an attacker exploited a reentrancy vulnerability in reward harvesting. The attacker registered a malicious fake Pendle market and manipulated reward accounting to drain staked assets. Penpie deployed post-audit code that permitted permissionless market registration and lacked reentrancy protection in batch reward harvesting. An attacker registered a fake market and triggered reentrancy to manipulate reward accounting, extracting excess rewards from legitimate pools.

On September 3, 2024, Penpie Protocol was exploited for approximately $27 million through a reentrancy vulnerability in its PendleStaking reward harvesting mechanism. The attacker leveraged permissionless market registration and a fake SY token, manipulating reward calculation and draining assets across Ethereum and Arbitrum. The batchHarvestMarketRewards() function of the PendleStaking contract lacked a reentrancy guard and trusted any market registered through Pendle's permissionless market factory. This allowed an attacker to deploy a malicious SY token, register a fake market, and re-enter the function to inflate reward balances, extracting excessive assets.

The defi protocol Penpie was exploited for 11,113.6 ETH (~$27.3 million) by an attacker who exploited a flaw allowing them to withdraw unearned "rewards". Although the protocol claimed to have been audited by two blockchain security firms, they later disclosed that the smart contracts containing the bugs had not been fully audited. The team behind Pendle (the platform on which Pendie is built) detected the attack and paused Pendle an hour after the attack began, which they claim prevented another $105 million from being stolen.
